pr.title: The UI's first version, implemented: transport and lanes over the files, with mute and solo
pr.head: 0ecfc4d5d3dd6e5dae9b8cd4a82dc37364d349e6

summary: Field is a Git-native music production tool: a song is a directory of YAML files, a build graph renders them into stems, and a native daemon, field-audiod, plays the result. Until this pull request, you worked with a song through CLI commands and hand edits. It adds field ui <song>, a desktop window onto a playing song.

The files stay the only store. field ui runs a local HTTP and WebSocket server inside field's own Node process, and a React client talks to it from an Electron window or a browser tab. Every gesture that changes the song ends as a YAML edit written through the same comment-preserving Document machinery the CLI's editors use. The existing watch loop then carries the file change into the playing session, exactly as it does for a hand edit. Each edit carries the sha256 of the file bytes it was derived from, so the server refuses a stale one and refreshes the view, and the server loads the project with the edited text before writing, so an edit that would add an error is refused instead of turning the song red.

• Mute. A new mute: field on a placement, beside gain_db and pan. The build graph leaves muted placements out of the plan, and a muted placement's sends go silent with it.
  • Solo. A session-only alternate feed: the server compiles a filtered copy of the song and swaps it into the daemon, and nothing is written.
  • Timeline. One row per placement, nested rows for placed tracks, waveforms, and clip move, split, and front and end trim.
  • Insert panel. Add, edit, and remove built-in effects on a track, with an EQ curve drawn by a TypeScript port of the native biquad arithmetic.
  • Plans. The UI plan flips to in-progress with a new §6, two other plans gain amendments, and a draft daw-features catalogue arrives, with its four picks as project stubs at priority: later.

The Projector review at 0ecfc4d requests changes with one P2: the CLI manual that main gained in #162, docs/cli.md, does not mention field ui. It is flagged on the command's registration in src/cli.ts. This pull request's own diff is unchanged since the clean review of ff0e86e, and all 23 earlier finding threads stay resolved. The author's own self-review threads are the author's to resolve. The head is untrusted, because its author has no write access to the repository, so the reviews read the code and ran none of it.

cards.title: Terms used on this page
cards.html:
• Placement or entry: one item in a track file's inputs: list, such as - track: drums or - audio: riff, with its position, length, level, and fades.
  • Lane or row: the timeline's drawing of one placement. Its entry is the placement's index in inputs:.
  • Send, receive, cable: a track's sends: feed a labelled cable, and a - receive: label entry in another track hears it, for example a shared reverb.
  • Stem: a track's rendered audio file. A frozen track is served to the daemon as its cached stem instead of being evaluated live.
  • Swap and ramp: the two ways the watch loop updates a playing session. A swap replaces the session, and a ramp moves one gain in place.
  • Carrier: under solo, a track the soloed track is heard through on its way to main.
  • Stale-hash guard: the check that an edit's sha256 still matches the file on disk.

cards.title: What each socket operation writes
cards.html:
OperationWritesInto
editgain_db, pan, or muteThe placement's owner file
moveat, in the author's spellingThe placement's owner file
splitTwo entries cloned from one, with duration, at, and source_offsetThe placement's owner file
stretchEnd: duration. Start: at, duration, and source_offsetThe placement's owner file
insert-add, insert-edit, insert-removeThe track's inserts: chainThe track's own file
soloNothing: the server swaps a filtered sessionNone
play, pause, stop, locate, deviceNothing: daemon transport commandsNone

groups.title: Mute and solo in the engine
groups.kicker: A placement field the build graph drops, and a filtered copy of the song for solo
intro: Mute is a boolean on a placement, stored in the file like gain_db. It is a field rather than a gain gesture because a gesture would overwrite the authored level, and remembering the old level anywhere but the file would be a second store. planFor in graph.ts filters muted placements out before anything else reads the track, so the stem's spec, its cache key, and the live session all leave them out. cables.ts walks each cable twice when a song has a muted placement: once with every placement, for structure and diagnostics, and once without the muted ones, for the arrivals that sound. A cable whose senders are all muted is silent, and graph.ts drops it as an input.

Solo is a listening gesture, so it lives in the running session and is never written. soloView in solo.ts walks the song and keeps three groups: the soloed track's own subtree, its carriers with only the inputs that lead to it, and the receivers of its sends. compileSession applies that filter to the loaded song before it builds the graph, and builds the session's files from that soloed graph, so a carrier frozen under the solo is served its soloed stem.
The build.ts changes are separate: they let a rebuild replace a stem that a Windows daemon holds open, and stop leaking temporary copies when it cannot.

files.note: Adds mute: z.boolean().default(false) to a placement, and puts mute after pan in the canonical key order.
The one-line filter in planFor that drops muted placements before the track is planned.
The solo walk: the soloed subtree, carriers, and send receivers, then applySolo filters each track's inputs and the cable list in place.
The second, audible pass of the arrival walk, which skips muted edges once the structural pass has decided whether the cable joins.
loadProject takes an optional override, one file's text as it would be, for a single synchronous load. field ui uses it to check an edit before writing.
compileSession takes solo, applies it to the loaded song before building the graph, and builds the session's files with build(project, graph, nodes) from that graph instead of reloading the files.

renameOverwrite retries a rename that Windows refuses while the daemon holds the stem open, and materialize skips the copy when the output already has the same bytes. The head's merge keeps this beside main's fetchAction.

groups.title: The wire protocol
groups.kicker: The messages between the server and the client, as TypeScript types
intro: ui-protocol.ts defines what the server sends down: a snapshot of the song, transport, devices, and timeline, daemon events such as position, and errors. The client imports the types, so a change to one side that the other cannot read fails the typecheck. The messages the client sends up are zod schemas in ui.ts, because the server must validate them.

files.note: The snapshot, event, and timeline-lane types. A lane's entry is the placement's index in its file's inputs:.

groups.title: Arithmetic the client shares with the engine
groups.kicker: Tempo and meter conversions and the EQ response, importable by the browser
intro: The client runs its own playhead between the daemon's 250 ms position events, so it needs the tempo and meter maps. It imports src/time/tempo.ts directly rather than porting it, so the two cannot drift. MeterMap gains position and span, the inverses of positionTicks and spanTicks, which the edits use to keep the author's bar-and-beat spelling.

The EQ editor redraws its curve during a drag, so eq-response.ts ports the native biquad design, magnitude, and auto-gain to TypeScript. The render still runs only in the daemon. A test holds the port equal to the C++ through a new eq-response mode in field-dsp-check.

files.note: Adds MeterMap.position, which turns ticks into [bar, beat, tick], and MeterMap.span, which turns ticks into a span from an anchor.
A line-for-line port of design, magnitudeDb, and autoGainDb from biquad.cpp, for drawing only.
An eq-response mode that prints the native curve and auto-gain for given bands, so a test can compare the port against it. cdd4388 added the <cmath> include that Linux needed.

groups.title: The field ui server
groups.kicker: One process that owns the session, the socket, and every write
intro: runUi compiles the session, connects to the daemon, and starts the watch loop. It then serves the built client and accepts WebSockets only on /ws, with a matching Origin and the per-launch token. Each message is validated with zod and dispatched: transport commands go to the daemon, and pause and stop push a snapshot with the transport's position. Solo recompiles and swaps the session, and holds the solo only once the swap succeeds. File edits run one at a time: each resolves the owner file, checks the hash, calls a pure function in ui-edits.ts, loads the project with the result, and writes it only when that load adds no error. Snapshots go out through their own promise chain and only when they differ.

At the end it opens the Electron shell, or a browser tab with --browser or when the shell exits before any view connects. It waits for Ctrl-C or for the window to close, then stops the transport and closes every open socket.

files.note: The server: upgrade guards, message schemas, the snapshot and write chains, writeChecked, the watch-loop hooks, the edit handlers, static files, the shell launch with its browser fallback, and teardown.
Registers field ui <song> with --port, --no-open, and --browser. The head's merge keeps it beside main's field record.

checks.text: P2 review finding: The new CLI manual, docs/cli.md, does not mention field ui. Fix: Add a short field ui section to docs/cli.md, covering how to open it, its three options, and the client build it needs, and add its row to the command reference.

groups.title: Edits and the timeline projection
groups.kicker: Pure text-to-text YAML edits, and the lanes the view draws
intro: ui-edits.ts holds every file edit as a pure function from document text to document text, so a test can write, read back, and compare bytes. Each one keeps the author's spelling: a musical at: [5] stays an array, defaults stay implicit, and comments survive. Split clones the entry node so both halves keep every field and comment.

ui-timeline.ts turns the loaded song into lanes: one per placement, children for placed tracks, each with its window in session samples, the hash of the file it came from, and a waveform envelope read from the built stem.

files.note: Edit, move, split, stretch, and the three insert operations, each returning the new text or a refusal.
Builds the timeline lanes and their waveform envelopes. 07447dd keeps each lane's index in the unfiltered inputs:, so a receive no longer shifts it.

checks.text: The receive-index fix holds at 0ecfc4d: placements() pairs each non-receive entry with its index in inputs: before filtering, at both the top level and the child rows. Checked by reading 07447dd and its new test.

groups.title: The client and its shell
groups.kicker: A React app in an Electron window, with local state only inside a gesture
intro: App.tsx opens the WebSocket, keeps the latest snapshot, and runs a frame loop that advances the playhead from the last position event. Timeline.tsx draws the ruler, rows, clips, waveforms, and drag handles, and follows the playhead during playback. Inserts.tsx shows the selected track's chain, with knobs for each effect and an EQ curve with draggable bands.
shell.cjs is the Electron main process: one window on the server's URL, with the renderer's console mirrored to the terminal, which is how a blank window was diagnosed.

files.note: The socket, the playhead loop that runs only while playing, the transport bar, the lane controls that write on pointer-up or key-up, and the keyboard shortcuts.
The timeline: rows, clip drags, trims, selection, and the follow-the-playhead scroll.
The insert panel: add and remove effects, knobs, and the EQ editor.
The Electron main process: profile directory, window, console mirroring, an http and https only window-open handler, and a will-navigate guard that keeps the window on the session.
Hand-rolled styles, including the sticky header column and the clip grips.
Mounts the app and turns a render crash into a visible message.
The page, with a content security policy limited to the local server.

groups.title: Workspace, dependencies, and CI
groups.kicker: A second pnpm workspace member for the client, and CI that builds it
intro: The client is its own pnpm workspace member, ui/, so its DOM and JSX toolchain stays out of the CLI's strict Node-only config. The root package gains ws for the server. React, Vite, and Electron live only in ui/. CI typechecks and builds the client on Linux.

files.note: Adds ws and @types/ws, and a build:ui script.
The client's dependencies: React 18, Vite 6, and Electron 43.
Declares the two workspace members, . and ui.
Builds ui/ on Linux, with a comment on why the install fetches no Electron runtime.
The Vite config, with only the React plugin, and a comment on why there is no dev-server mode against a running field ui.
The client's own TypeScript config, with DOM types and JSX.

groups.title: Root docs
groups.kicker: How mute and field ui work, in the docs that describe the system today
intro: The root docs describe the system as it is, and the repository asks for them to change in the same pull request as the behavior. tracks.md adds mute to what an entry can carry, build-graph.md says how a muted entry leaves the plan and its cables, and architecture.md describes field ui: the loopback server, its guards, the session-only solo, and the shell.

files.note: mute among an entry's fields, and what it does to the placement and its sends.
A muted entry leaves the stem's spec, key, and dependencies, and an all-muted cable carries nothing.
A paragraph on field ui in the control plane section.

groups.title: Plans
groups.kicker: The UI plan flips to in-progress, two plans record amendments, and a catalogue arrives
intro: The UI plan, docs/projects/ui/readme.md, moves from draft to in-progress at priority: now and gains §6, the record of what the first implementation settled, including the four §3 non-goals the first version crossed: the timeline, its waveforms, the clip edits, and the insert editor. Every question in §5 is answered or settled, so the flip owes no open question. project-core §5 records the new stack pieces, the ui/ workspace member, ws, React, Vite, and Electron, against its single-package decision. render-pipeline decision 4 records the TypeScript EQ arithmetic as a bounded reversal.

daw-features is a draft catalogue of what users of other DAWs praise and wish for, with what each would mean for Field. It claims no readiness. Its four picks now have project directories of their own at draft and later: detail-pane, actions-and-macros, sound-browser, and key-conforming. Each is a stub with a goal and a pointer back to its catalogue section, as the repository asks of a project with no plan yet.

files.note: Frontmatter flip, §5's shell question settled, and §6, which now records the nested rows, the timeline, the clip edits, and the insert editor with their reasons.
Two dated amendments to §5's stack record: the workspace member with ws, React, and Vite, and then Electron, which downloads its runtime on first use.
An amendment to decision 4: response arithmetic, never sample processing, exists in TypeScript again, held equal to the C++ by a test.
A draft research catalogue at priority: later. §16 links each of its four picks to its new project.
